assets.prompt: Continuous handheld point-of-view video shot out of the open passenger window of a moving car at night on a two-lane road north of a city, roughly forty-five seconds, 24fps cinematic look, ultra-high-definition. For about the first two-thirds: a very dark, low-key, near-black nocturnal scene, wet black asphalt reflecting widely spaced warm sodium-amber street lamps, a faint double-yellow line, the car's low-beam headlights pooling on the road ahead; the ROAD and the lit lane sit well LEFT of centre in the frame for almost the whole shot while the dark treeline and shoulder fill the right side, so a centre crop would miss the road entirely; slow, steady, quiet motion, deep shadows, heavy grain, the mood of driving home very late. Then in the final third the car enters a LIT road tunnel: the exposure ramps up hard and the whole frame becomes much BRIGHTER, rows of white ceiling lights streak past fast and close, high motion energy and speed, pale tiled walls flaring, visually the brightest and most motion-dense passage of the entire clip and tonally the opposite of the dark sodium-road mood. Realistic imperfect handheld footage with slight camera shake, no on-screen text, no readable license plates, no visible faces, no real brand logos.

One take, out the passenger window, north of the city, around eleven at night. Maybe forty-five seconds, the whole thing. These are the bits I keep coming back to. The positions are rough — I did them from memory on the couch, so go by the picture, not by my numbers.

LAYOUT SPEC for NIGHTFORM's label printer's existing sleeve-card press PDF (flat, single record, from the previous release; to be reverse-engineered downstream into a live merge template).

Document: single sleeve card, 105 x 148 mm PORTRAIT (A6), NO bleed box present (trim = media box, 0 mm bleed), fonts embedded. This is the only artefact the printer still holds from the last release.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (reads as a wordmark plus four separate lines, one column, centred over pale board):
- Head: the NIGHTFORM WORDMARK, placed as artwork, centred at the top, with a thin amber rule beneath it.
- Line 1: TITLE LINE — 'Nightfall Drive' — in a display grotesque sans, large.
- Line 2: CATALOGUE NUMBER — 'NF-006' — small.
- Line 3: FORMAT — '12-inch vinyl' — small.
- Line 4: RELEASE DATE — 'Released March 2024' — small.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- The TITLE, CATALOGUE NUMBER, FORMAT and DATE are a SINGLE continuous text story in ONE text frame, separated only by line breaks, NOT four separately addressable frames — so the conversion exposes nothing like the per-line frame structure the printed card implies, and there is no per-field frame to bind each merge value into.
- The wordmark at the head is a PLACED IMAGE (the flat black plate), not text.
- So the frame inventory a conversion exposes (roughly one flowing text frame + one placed image + the amber rule) is nothing like the four tidy fields the printed card suggests; every field past the title has to be reached as a position inside one reconstructed story.
- Compounding it: the readout a field map would be computed from OMITS ONE RUN (the FORMAT line, '12-inch vinyl') while KEEPING its line break, so the reconstructed story string still looks well-formed at four lines, every character offset past that point is short by the length of the omitted run, and the mapping validator returns valid with no warning.

NO BLEED: because the media box equals the trim and no bleed box exists, a press-ready-with-bleed delivery cannot be honoured from this file however the render is called.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens): TITLE_LINE | CATALOGUE_NO | FORMAT | RELEASE_DATE

Colours: Tunnel White #E8E4DC board, Asphalt Black #0C0E12 type, Sodium Amber #C77A2E rule under the wordmark.
